newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria car bomb kills five, wounds 15.
newsitem.headline: Algeria car bomb kills five, wounds 15.

text.p: A car bomb explosion killed five people and wounded 15 in the Algerian garrison town of Blida near Algiers on Sunday, Algerian security forces announced in a statement.
The blast, four days before Algerians vote on changing the constitution, jolted Blida at about 9.20 a.m. (0820 GMT), said the statement carried by the official Algerian news agenct APS.
The explosion killed five people and wounded 15, the statement said without giving other details.
The military headquarters for Algiers and neighbouring towns are located in Bilda, 50 km (30 miles) south of the capital.

The bomb attack followed a series of raids and mass killing of civilians which the Algerian authorities blame on Moslem rebels waging a five-year-old guerrilla struggle against the North African state.
More than 120 people, including children and women, have been killed in the past six weeks, according to independent sources in Algiers.
Algerian newspapers have dubbed the month leading to the November 28 referendum the "Month of all horrors".
The draft constitution bans politicians from using Islam, among other things, as a weapon to gain power.
Algerian residents said the authorities had tightened security in the past week to pre-empt guerrillas attacks, deploying more soliders and mobile patrols in and around main cities.
Algeria's Armed Islamic Group (GIA), blamed for killing civilians, last week warned Algerians that its guerrillas would "strike the neck" of any one who dared leaving his home to vote.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when army-backed authorities scrapped a general election in whihc radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
